doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Europe and Japan's respect for the music
summary: Popularity in Europe and Japan where musicians are treated like royalty.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Does this kind of music that you play fly in Europe?

Oh yeah, yeah. And you know the one tour that I didn’t do with Soulive was the European tour. I haven’t had a chance to go to Europe yet, but I know that it’s definitely very popular — more so than here I think. And Japan, again.

That’s been like that for years because even the guys that were playing in the forties and fifties, they used to say that, and now that they’re older they say that in Japan they were treated like real artists or something.

That’s what I’ve been trying to say, yeah. They open the doors for you. They’re like, “Here they come.” You know what I mean? Yeah. It’s something we haven’t experienced as musicians, you’re like royalty over there. It’s just a higher level of playing.
It’s interesting, when things come from somewhere else we seem to value them more I guess.
Yeah and so much of that is right here in front of them.
